VZ.rationale: VZ presents a moderately attractive case anchored by a genuine earnings improvement that the market has not yet priced in. Q1 2026 delivered a beat: EPS of $1.28 vs $1.21 consensus, adjusted EBITDA margin at a record 38.9%, and the first positive Q1 postpaid phone net adds in 13 years (+55K, a ~340K YoY improvement). Trailing net margin jumped from 0.076 to 0.128 as the Q1 filing was absorbed, and the trailing P/E compressed to 11.4x — the floor of its 365-day range (11.0–21.2x) — versus a prior 12-month average near 17–18x. This compression is mechanically driven by only one quarter of new data being embedded (TTM not available per pack), so the cheapness thesis depends on Q1 being representative of the full-year run-rate. However, management raised adjusted EPS growth guidance to 5–6% (from 4–5%) and reaffirmed FCF guidance of ~$21.5B, providing some corroboration. The 8.7% earnings yield offers a 414bps spread over the 10Y Treasury (4.57%), and the ~6% dividend yield provides income support. The primary concern is the ~$34B increase in liabilities (driven largely by the ~$20B Frontier acquisition), pushing D/E to ~3.0x and leverage to ~2.6x net debt/EBITDA, with a deleveraging target of 2.0–2.25x by 2027. Wireless service revenue declined ~1% YoY in Q1, though management characterized it as the trough. The narrow-moat franchise in a rational oligopoly, combined with cost-reduction targets ($5B OpEx savings by end-2026, $1B Frontier synergies by 2028), supports a stable earnings trajectory. The score of +0.35 reflects solid fundamentals with improving trajectory, meaningful valuation discount vs own history, and a modest near-term catalyst from the raised guidance and FIFA World Cup customer acquisition push — but tempered by elevated leverage, single-quarter P/E data, and constrained pricing power in a promotional market.
